antidotes.why: Better to follow one's own path imperfectly.

antidotes.source: Manas Uttar 38; Yoga Vasishtha Bhushunda; Gita 12.13
antidotes.why: The good are gladdened by others' joy.
Content with what comes, beyond envy.

chains.summary: The envious, the scornful, the discontented, the quick to anger, the ever suspicious, and the one who lives on another's fortune are always in sorrow.
chains.title: Six who are always unhappy

verses.m: The envious, the scornful, the discontented, the short-tempered, the ever-suspicious, and one who lives off another's fortune: these six are always unhappy.
verses.sa: ईर्षुर्धृणी नसन्तुष्टः क्रोधनो नित्यशङ्कितः / परभाग्योपजीवी च षडेते नित्यदुःखिताः

verses.m: Delusion is the root of all diseases, and from it spring many pains. Desire is the wind, greed the endless phlegm, and anger the bile that keeps the chest burning.
verses.sa: मोह सकल ब्याधिन्ह कर मूला। तिन्ह ते पुनि उपजहिं बहु सूला॥ काम बात कफ लोभ अपारा। क्रोध पित्त नित छाती जारा ॥

verses.m: Possessiveness is ringworm and envy is the itch; the swings of elation and dejection are throat ailments. The burning you feel at another's happiness is consumption, and malice and a crooked mind are leprosy.
verses.sa: ममता दादु कंडु इरषाई। हरष बिषाद गरह बहुताई॥ पर सुख देखि जरनि सोइ छई। कुष्ट दुष्टता मन कुटिलई ॥

refs: Mahabharata, Shanti Parva (Narada to Shuka, quoting Sanatkumara)
chains.summary: You should guard your discipline from anger, your fortune from envy, your learning from pride and slight, and yourself from heedlessness.
chains.title: Guard each thing from its thief

verses.m: Always guard your discipline from anger and your good fortune from envy; guard your learning from both pride and insult, and guard yourself from carelessness.
verses.sa: नित्यं क्रोधात्तपो रक्षेच्छ्रियं रक्षेच्च मत्सरात् / विद्यां मानावमानाभ्यामात्मानं तु प्रमादतः

depicts.m: They say ruin is born of jealousy; even ascetics fall to it. Jealousy threw me into a sea of wrongdoing.
depicts.sa: ईर्ष्याजं व्यसनं प्राहुस्तेन चैवोर्ध्वरेतसः / ईर्ष्यया त्वहमाक्षिप्तो मग्नो दुष्कृतसागरे
depicts.why: Irshya named by the one it overcame.

depicts.m: One who envies others their wealth, looks, strength, family, happiness, good fortune or honours suffers from a disease without end.
depicts.sa: य ईर्षुः परवित्तेषु रूपे वीर्ये कुलान्वये / सुखसौभाग्यसत्कारे तस्य व्याधिरनन्तकः
depicts.why: Shows envy fixing on exactly what it lists.

gloss: The Manas calls burning at another's good an itch and a wasting disease. Vidura calls it an illness without end.

heals.m: One who hates no being, who is friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and ego, even in pain and pleasure, and forgiving,
heals.sa: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च । निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी ॥

heals.m: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
heals.sa: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
heals.why: Names one's own imperfect path outranking a perfect copy of someone else's.

heals.m: Better is one's own duty, even done imperfectly, than the duty of another well done. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is full of fear.
heals.sa: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
heals.why: Names one's own imperfect path outranking a perfect copy of someone else's.

heals.m: We are content here with bark garments, you with silk; the contentment is equal, and the difference makes no difference. He is poor whose craving is vast. When the mind is content, who is rich and who is poor?
heals.sa: वयमिह परितुष्टा वल्कलैस्त्वं दुकूलैः सम इव परितोषो निर्विशेषो विशेषः । स तु भवतु दरिद्रो यस्य तृष्णा विशाला मनसि च परितुष्टे कोऽर्थवान्को दरिद्रः ॥
heals.why: Shows silk and bark giving the same contentment.

heals.m: They are not greedy for pleasures; they are mines of good conduct and virtue; others' sorrow makes them sad and others' joy makes them glad. They are even-minded, see no one as an enemy, are free of pride and detached, and have let go of greed, rage, elation and fear.
heals.sa: बिषय अलंपट सील गुनाकर। पर दुख दुख सुख सुख देखे पर॥ सम अभूतरिपु बिमद बिरागी। लोभामरष हरष भय त्यागी ॥
heals.why: Another's joy is felt as one's own.

heals.m: One who sees all beings in the self, and the self in all beings, no longer shrinks away from anyone.
heals.sa: यस्तु सर्वाणि भूतान्यात्मन्येवानुपश्यति । सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं ततो न विजुगुप्सते ॥
heals.why: There is no second person to measure against.

heals.m: I am happy when people are happy and sad when people are sad; I am a dear friend to all. So I live long, free of illness.
heals.sa: सुखितोऽस्मि सुखापन्ने दुःखितो दुःखिते जने । सर्वस्य प्रियमित्रं च तेन जीवाम्यनामयः ॥
heals.why: Shows others' joy is shared, not compared.

heals.m: The world is covered by ignorance; it does not shine because of envy; people abandon friends out of greed, and miss heaven through attachment.
heals.r: Hamsa Gita 40 (Mahabharata, Shanti 12.305.40 in our data)
heals.sa: अज्ञानेनावृतो लोको मात्सर्यान्न प्रकाशते । लोभात्त्यजति मित्राणि सङ्गात्स्वर्गं न गच्छति ॥
heals.why: Names envy as what dims us.

hero.m: Content with whatever comes unasked, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy, the same in success and failure, even when acting he is not bound.
hero.sa: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः । समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥

loci.m: Content with whatever comes unasked, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy, the same in success and failure, even when acting he is not bound.
loci.sa: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः । समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥

loci.m: One who envies others their wealth, looks, strength, family, happiness, good fortune or honours suffers from a disease without end.
loci.sa: य ईर्षुः परवित्तेषु रूपे वीर्ये कुलान्वये / सुखसौभाग्यसत्कारे तस्य व्याधिरनन्तकः

loci.m: Possessiveness is ringworm and envy is the itch; the swings of elation and dejection are throat ailments. The burning you feel at another's happiness is consumption, and malice and a crooked mind are leprosy.
loci.sa: ममता दादु कंडु इरषाई। हरष बिषाद गरह बहुताई॥ पर सुख देखि जरनि सोइ छई। कुष्ट दुष्टता मन कुटिलई ॥

practices.m: Friend mind, what is the use of so much chatter? Friend mind, all this is mere speculation. I have told you the heart of it: you are reality itself, vast as the sky.
practices.sa: सखे मनः किं बहुजल्पितेन सखे मनः सर्वमिदं वितर्क्यम् । यत्सारभूतं कथितं मया ते त्वमेव तत्त्वं गगनोपमोऽसि ॥

practices.m: Wealth has three destinies: giving, enjoying and loss. Whoever neither gives nor enjoys it meets the third.
practices.sa: दानं भोगो नाशस्तिस्रो गतयो भवन्ति वित्तस्य । यो न ददाति न भुङ्क्ते तस्य तृतीया गतिर्भवति ॥

practices.m: Wish for what can be had, never for what cannot. Enjoy what is in front of you now, and do not grieve over what has not yet come.
practices.why: Shows enjoying what is present is named as the practice.

practices.m: No one in this world gains real wealth through greed. Enough of greed, my son. Be at peace.
practices.r: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
practices.sa: न लोभादर्थसंपत्तिर्नराणामिह दृश्यते / तदलं तात लोभेन प्रशाम्य भरतर्षभ ॥

practices.m: The seventh is to see the whole world as filled with me, and to regard good people as greater than me. The eighth is to be content with whatever comes, and never, even in a dream, to look for faults in others.
practices.sa: सातवँ सम मोहि मय जग देखा। मोतें संत अधिक करि लेखा॥ आठवँ जथालाभ संतोषा। सपनेहुँ नहिं देखइ परदोषा ॥
practices.why: Shows contentment named as a form of devotion.

practices.m: Will I ever live like this? By the grace of kind Raghunath, will I take on the nature of a saint: always content with what comes, wanting nothing from anyone, always devoted to others' good, keeping my vow in mind, deed and word; hearing very harsh words and not burning in that fire; free of pride, even and cool of mind, speaking of others' virtues and not their faults; letting go of the body's worries, bearing joy and sorrow with an even mind?
practices.sa: कबहुँक हौं यहि रहनि रहौंगो। श्रीरघुनाथ-कृपालु-कृपातें संत-सुभाव गहौंगो॥ ९॥ जथालाभसंतोष सदा, काहू सों कछु न चहांगो। पर-हित-निरत निरंतर, मन क्रम बचन नेम निबहौंगो॥ … परुष बचन अति दुसह श्रवन सुनि तेहि पावक न दहांगो। बिगत मान, सम सीतल मन, पर-गुन नहिं दोष कहाँगो॥ ३॥ परिहरि देह-जनित चिंता, दुख-सुख समबुद्धि सहोंगो।

practices.m: In a vessel full of awakening, filled with the oil of detachment and fitted with the wick of devotion, behold the lamp of knowing. In the hollow darkness of delusion it rises of itself. Make detachment the lower fire-stick and knowledge the upper.
practices.sa: स होवाच । वैराग्यतैलसम्पूर्णे भक्तिवर्तिसमन्विते । प्रबोधपूर्णपात्रे तु ज्ञप्तिदीपं विलोकयेत् ॥ मोहान्धकारे निःसारे उदेति स्वयमेव हि । वैराग्यमरणिं कृत्वा ज्ञानं कृत्वोत्तरारणिम् ॥
practices.why: Shows the light then rises of itself.

practices.m: Four gatekeepers are named at the door of freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment, and the company of good people. Take refuge in even one of them with full effort, setting all else aside; when one is won, all four come under your control.
practices.sa: मोक्षद्वारे द्वारपालश्चत्वारः परिकीर्तिताः । शमो विचारः सन्तोषश्चतुर्थः साधुसङ्गमः ॥ एकं वा सर्वयत्नेन सर्वमुत्सृज्य संश्रयेत् । एकस्मिन्वशगे यान्ति चत्वारोऽपि वशं गताः ॥
practices.why: Contentment is named as a door, not a reward.

stories.l: When the mind is content, nobody is richer than you.
stories.s: An ascetic tells a king who ignores him that learning equals wealth, that contentment in bark equals contentment in silk, and that pride over a few towns is a fever.
stories.t: Vairagyashatakam: Dialogue between the ascetic and the king

stories.l: The quiet one everyone relies on often matters most.
stories.s: Speech, sight, hearing and mind each claim to be the most important. Their father says the greatest is the one whose absence hurts the body most. Each leaves for a year and the body manages; when breath starts to leave, all the others are torn loose and beg it to stay.
stories.t: The senses argue over who is greatest

stories.l: Your fear of someone else's goodness usually says more about your interests than theirs.
stories.s: Indra, king of the gods, fears that Bharat's devotion will bring Ram back and spoil the gods' plans, and wants to trick him. His teacher Brihaspati tells him that the world runs on action, that harming a good person backfires, and that his anxiety comes from his own self-interest, not from Bharat.

stories.l: Insecurity shows in how we size up rivals before anything has happened.
stories.s: The blind king Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what happened at Kurukshetra. Sanjaya describes Duryodhana going to Drona and nervously naming the great warriors on both sides.
stories.t: The great warriors of both armies are named
